newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares flat as foreigners stay away.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares flat as foreigners stay away.

text.p: Norwegian shares were mainly flat on Thursday in dull trade and dealers said a lack of foreign interest was weighing on the market.
Oslo's Total share index edged down 0.3 percent to end at 1,117.60 points in turnover of 1.07 billion crowns.

"There's no foreign interest in the market at the moment. There's no sense of direction, it's flat and the volume is not so high," said one dealer. "The market needs more liquidity from abroad to get a lift."

More than three million crowns of the session's total turnover was due to trade in Fokus Bank, which is currently locked in a battle with Den norske Bank for mortgage lender BNbank, and is itself is the target of a takeover by Sparebankgruppen.
Fokus advanced 11 percent, or seven crowns, to close at 70 crowns. Dealers said it was unclear who the counterparties were in the Fokus trade.
Telecommunications group Nera continued to attract interest and accounted for 92 million crowns of business. Nera's stock finished 1.50 crowns higher at 42.50 crowns.
